title: Assembled temp_por_top supply current (Iq) in the por-iq, temp-iq (incremental) and iq-total states across the 45-point PVT grid
claim: Issue #107 -- EVIDENCE ONLY, NOT a spec claim and NOT a proposed ceiling (DR-003 row 7 TBD-4/5/6 are owned by a follow-on decision record that would use this result). Records the settled VDD supply current of the unchanged assembled design/netlist/temp_por_top.spice (as drawn: bias_core + temp_core + por_comparator + por_output_chain with the real shared IBIAS node and the real RESETn -> temp_core.EN feedback) in two directly simulated states -- por-iq (RESETn asserted/low, which disables temp_core) and iq-total (natural released state) -- and the derived incremental temp-iq = iq-total - por-iq, over {tt, ss, ff, sf, fs} x {-40, 27, 125 C} x {2.97, 3.30, 3.63 V}. iq-total is measured in its own simulation and is NOT a sum; the per-sub-cell currents are attribution only, taken from the same runs, and the direct-vs-attribution-sum discrepancy is reported (spec/porting-plan.md Sec1.1). Every grid point carries an explicit status (ok / non-physical-branch / unsettled / nonconverged).
provenance_source: sim/iq-top/testbench/tb_temp_por_iq_{por,total}.sch (DUT: design/netlist/temp_por_top.spice, the committed export of design/temp_por_top.sch)
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix measurement, not a distribution claim)

por-iq.description: RESETn asserted (low). RESETn is a DUT output that releases by itself once VDD is above VPOR-rise, so it is held low by a 0 V forcing voltage source (VRST: RESETn -> VSS) added in the TESTBENCH; the DUT netlist is not altered. VRST's own current is not part of the VDD measurement. The contention current -- the output stage's pull-up (MOP/MAST) pushing RESETn high against the force -- flows VDD -> MOP -> RESETn -> VRST, is therefore INCLUDED in -i(BVDD), and is read separately as i(VRST) and reported; por-iq less that contention is also reported. temp_core.EN follows RESETn (low), so temp_core is disabled.

iq-total.description: Natural released state: RESETn left to the DUT (released after the one-shot, temp_core enabled by RESETn). Measured directly in its own simulation, never as por-iq + temp-iq.

measurement.status: EXPLORATORY measurement definitions chosen for this campaign; none is a ratified bound.
measurement.method: Transient from a physical 0 V start (the same branch-selecting method as sim/supply-ramp-top and sim/temp-core-startup, not a cold .op). V(VDD) = min(final_supply, rate*t) at a fast constant rate, then held constant. Supply current I = -i(BVDD). Ramp coverage is sim/supply-ramp-top; this campaign measures a SETTLED current at constant VDD.

settling.note: A point is `ok` only if the mean current of the trailing window differs from the previous window's mean by <= max_window_to_window_drift (relative), the trailing window's peak-to-peak is <= max_trailing_window_pk_pk of its mean, VDD sits within vdd_tolerance_v of the target, and the state is the one asked for (iq-total: RESETn released > 0.8*VDD; por-iq: RESETn <= 0.05 V). Otherwise `unsettled` -- never PASS-by-default.

non_physical_branch.signature: design/temp_core.md (issue #19 / #22 signature, about lines 145-172) and the issue #86 outcome: any saved node outside [-0.3 V, VDD+0.5 V] in the trailing window (e.g. PTAT/CTAT railed far outside every other corner's range), a settled total supply current <= 0, or a settled sub-cell supply current below -1 nA. #86 is still open at the time of writing; if it resolves differently the status rule here follows #86's result in a superseding record.

measurement.attribution_instrumentation: Four 0 V voltage sources (vsbias, vscmp, vspor, vstemp) are inserted by the driver into the generated deck, in series with each sub-cell instance's VDD pin inside the temp_por_top subcircuit (text edit of the four instance lines, each asserted to match exactly once). A 0 V source adds no resistance, so the DUT circuit is electrically unchanged; the same instrumented deck is used for both states and the total is still the independent -i(BVDD). Attribution is per sub-cell (por_output_chain includes MASSIST); it is never summed into iq-total, only compared with it.

ngspice_note: The fleet runner (klt 0.5.0, ngspice 46) ignores options.ngspice_init and expr measurements, so the equivalent of sim/spiceinit's ng_nomodcheck is set by a .control block carried in the netlist body ('set ng_nomodcheck'). Local ngspice is 42; a single-point local cross-check is recorded.

solver_sensitivity.scope: iq-total (natural release) only, full 45-point grid per variant. Forced-low por-iq contention and the definition of incremental temp-iq are separate DR-006 blockers and are not addressed. Evidence only: no Iq ceiling is proposed and no ratified row changes.

baseline.description: Control: the unchanged generated deck of record 20261009-191705-df85523 (testbench `.options method=gear trtol=50`, tmax 10 us, default reltol). Re-run in this campaign so every variant is compared against a same-campaign control as well as against the original record.

trtol7.description: Tighter local-truncation-error acceptance: `.options method=gear trtol=7` (the #86 / #142 discriminator of the same name). Replaces only the testbench options line.

reltol2e-4.description: Tighter relative tolerance: `.options method=gear trtol=50 reltol=2e-4` (the #86 / #142 discriminator of the same name). Replaces only the testbench options line.

solver_sensitivity.unchanged_across_variants: DUT, testbench, supply source, analysis card (1u step, 30 ms, tmax 10 us), measurement windows, all settling/physicality thresholds (the `measurement` block above), and the grid grading code (iq_checker.grade on the full-resolution waveform).

comparison_criterion.rule: Two physical (`ok`) settled currents at the same corner AGREE iff |I_a - I_b| / min(I_a, I_b) <= 0.01 (1 %). A corner with >= 2 `ok` landings among {baseline, trtol7, reltol2e-4} AGREES iff the max pairwise relative difference is <= 0.01.
comparison_criterion.rationale: Fixed before any result was seen and independent of observed outcomes: 0.01 is the existing `settling.max_window_to_window_drift`, i.e. the repo's own definition of 'the same settled current' for one run; two solver settings that land on the same physical branch should reproduce a settled current at least as well as one run reproduces itself between adjacent windows. It is a measurement-equivalence band, not a spec limit. The smallest current is never selected and no variant is treated as authoritative.

classification_of_original_exclusions.population: the points with status != ok for iq-total in record 20261009-191705-df85523 (17 of 45)
rules_in_order: unresolved: any of the three runs has no graded result (fleet refusal, missing waveform, invalid waveform -> nonconverged) AND no run is `ok`.
unresolved (physical-disagreement): >= 2 `ok` runs whose currents do not all agree within agreement_rel_tol.

recovered-solver-sensitive: >= 1 run is `ok` and all `ok` runs agree within agreement_rel_tol. This records that a physical settled landing EXISTS under that setting; it does not prove the original artifact's cause, and any non-ok run at the same point is listed beside it.
reproduced-non-physical: all three runs returned a graded result and every one is non-physical-branch.
physical-failure: all three runs returned a graded result, none is non-physical-branch, none is ok (physical landing that fails the unchanged settling/state checks).
unresolved (mixed): anything else (e.g. non-physical in some runs and unsettled in others, no ok run).

solver_sensitivity.new_failure_rule: A point that was `ok` in the original record and is not `ok` in any run of this campaign is reported as newly failing, with the run(s) and status.
